# A yen balance bought at a rate no fixed number of decimals states exactly.
#
# ¥2,000,000 for 18,200.01 CAD is 0.0091000050 CAD/JPY. Written as a rate to
# eight places and multiplied back out, the value lands a cent either side of
# 18,200.01 depending on which way the eighth digit goes — and the CAD side
# carries no rate, so it comes back exact and the entry no longer sums to
# zero. GnuCash then parks the difference in an Imbalance split.
#
# The figures are ordinary: ¥2,000,000 is about CAD 18,200, which is a bank
# balance, not an edge case. What makes it bite is the size — the error is
# bounded by the amount times half of the last place kept, so it passes half a
# cent somewhere around a million units.
#
# JPY has no minor unit, so the amount is a whole number of yen and the
# `share_price:` states the rate as the exact ratio it is.
#
# Verified by tests/integration/test_beancount_keeps_the_units_the_book_holds.py.
2026-01-01 commodity CAD
	mnemonic: "CAD"
	fullname: "Canadian Dollar"
	namespace: "CURRENCY"
	fraction: 100
2026-01-01 commodity JPY
	mnemonic: "JPY"
	fullname: "Japanese Yen"
	namespace: "CURRENCY"
	fraction: 1
2026-01-01 open Assets
	type: Asset
	commodity.namespace: "CURRENCY"
	commodity.mnemonic: "CAD"
2026-01-01 open Assets:Bank
	type: Bank
	commodity.namespace: "CURRENCY"
	commodity.mnemonic: "CAD"
2026-01-01 open Assets:Bank:JPY
	type: Bank
	commodity.namespace: "CURRENCY"
	commodity.mnemonic: "JPY"

2026-02-01 * "Buy 2,000,000 JPY"
	currency.mnemonic: "CAD"
	Assets:Bank:JPY 2000000 JPY
		account.commodity.mnemonic: "JPY"
		share_price: "1820001/200000000"
		value: "18200.01"
	Assets:Bank -18200.01 CAD
		account.commodity.mnemonic: "CAD"
